newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro stocks hit records; dollar, pound rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro stocks hit records; dollar, pound rise.

text.p: A record close on Wall Street, the world's largest stock market, helped spur the London and Frankfurt bourses to new peaks in morning trading on Tuesday.
The dollar and pound also gained ground, aided by the rally in share prices and pressure on the yen from dearer oil.

The Dow Jones industrial average ended above 6,000 for the first time on Monday, cheered by a healthy U.S. economic outlook and a jump in oil prices to the highest level since the Gulf War, which fuelled a rise in oil shares.
London's stock market, Europe's busiest, had already breached the 4,000 mark on the FTSE 100 share index and made further progress in early trading.
"There's no doubt we're going higher today," said one London share dealer. "But I don't expect anything too dramatic."

London shares have followed in the slipstream of U.S. markets since late July amid indications that U.S. interest rates, a key influence on other world markets, were not likely to rise in the near future.
Germany's DAX index opened at a record high above 2,700 and added to its gains, boosted by the Wall Street close, higher bond prices and strength in the dollar -- good news for German exporters.
The Paris bourse was near its highs for the year, led by gains in oil stocks.

The 30-share Dow jumped 40.62 points to 6,010.00. It had topped the 6,000 mark during trading last week but failed to end above that key psychological level, seen as important for market sentiment. In a dizzying rise, it soared through 5,000 only last November, nine months after topping 4,000.
Traders said higher-than-expected profits from computer chip giant Intel, announced after the New York close, could give a further boost to shares.

But they cautioned that investors might hold back ahead of a new trading day on Wall Street as Monday's gains were won in muted trading, when the U.S. bond market was shut for the Columbus Day holiday.
They may also wait to see British and U.S. economic figures later in the week, particularly U.S. September consumer price (CPI) data on Wednesday.
"U.S. CPI is the big one," said one London trader. "People will not want to stick their neck out too much ahead of that."
"The dollar continues to stalk recent peaks against the yen and the mark and we'd look for it to break higher near-term," said Peter Von Maydell, senior currency economist at UBS.

A rise in oil prices to five-year highs weakened the yen, in view of Japan's dependence on imported oil, while helping to send the pound to 21-month highs against the mark, 11-month peaks versus the dollar and three-year highs against the yen.
"Sterling's broken all our near-term targets and it could go a lot further, possibly to 2.48 marks," said a U.S. bank trader.
The yen also attracted some uncertainty ahead of Sunday's Japanese general election.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5362 marks and 112.17 yen, compared with 1.5293 and 111.60 in late European business on Monday. The pound gained to $1.5839 and 2.4272 marks from $1.5805 and 2.4174.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 19.6 points at 4,058.3.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was 31.46 ahead at 2,725.34.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was 18.22 higher at 2,161.84.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $381 an ounce on Tuesday morning, compared with Monday's London close of $381.65 and afternoon fix of $380.90. Silver slipped three cents to $5.02.
